title: Synthesis of substituted morpholines using stereodivergent aza-Michael reactions catalyzed by Bronsted acids
authors: Zhong, Cheng; Wang, Yikai; O'Herin, Conor; Young, Damian W.
reference: Synthesis of substituted morpholines using stereodivergent aza-Michael reactions catalyzed by Bronsted acids | Zhong, Cheng; Wang, Yikai; O'Herin, Conor; Young, Damian W. | ACS Catalysis (2013), 3(4), 643-646
experimental_procedure: To a round bottom flask equipped with magnetic stir bar, L-tyrosine (200 mg, 1.2 mmol) was added and dissolved in DMF (8.0 mL, 0.15 M) followed by the addition of EtN3 (157 mg, 1.56 mmol, 1.3 eq.) and DMAP (7.5 mg, 0.06 mmol, 0.05 eq.). The reaction flask was cooled in ice water for 15 minutes and CbzCl (224 mg, 1.32 mmol, 1.1 eq.) was added drop wise over 5 minutes. The reaction was monitored by TLC and until the starting material was consumed over 5 hours. The mixture was diluted with EtOAc (100 mL) and washed by HCl solution (1.0 M), saturated NaHCO3 (aq.), brine and then dried over anhydrous Na2SO4. The solvent was removed under reduced pressure to give the crude residue. Without column purification, the crude Z-tyrosine was dissolved in DMF (8 mL, 0.15 M) and MeI (186 mg, 1.32 mmol, 1.1 eq.) was added. Next, oven dried K2CO3 (882 mg, 6.0 mmol, 5 eq.) was added to the reaction mixture was stirred for 10 hours, based on TLC consumption of the starting material. The mixture was diluted with EtOAc (100 mL), washed with HCl solution (1.0 M), saturated NaHCO3 (aq.), brine and then dried over anhydrous Na2SO4. The solvent was removed under reduced pressure to give the crude residue. Flash silica gel chromatography (Ethyl Acetate/Hexane 40:60) was then applied to give the protected amino alcohol. 285 mg (75% yield).
notes: chemoselective (stages 1+2), intermediate Cbz-protected substrate from stage 1 added in stage 2, dropwise addition of Cbz-Cl (stage 1, substage 1)

authors: Golobokova, T. V.; Pokatilov, F. A.; Proidakov, A. G.; Kazantseva, M. V.; Shevchenko, G. G.; Vereshchagin, L. I.; Kizhnyaev, V. N.
reference: Synthesis of polynuclear azoles linked through carbamate and urea bridges | Golobokova, T. V.; Pokatilov, F. A.; Proidakov, A. G.; Kazantseva, M. V.; Shevchenko, G. G.; Vereshchagin, L. I.; Kizhnyaev, V. N. | Russian Journal of Organic Chemistry (2012), 48(4), 566-574
experimental_procedure: General/Typical Procedure: 2-Phenyl-2H-1,2,3-triazole-4-carbonyl azide (VIIa). Acid chloride XIIa, 5 g (24 mmol), was added in portions under vigorous stirring at room temperature to a mixture of 2.4 g (37 mmol) of sodium azide, 25 ml of water, 0.2 g of benzyltriethylammonium chloride (BTEAC), and 35 ml of diethyl ether. The mixture was stirred for 3 h until XIIa disappeared (TLC), the organic phase was separated, and the aqueous phase was extracted with diethyl ether (5 × 35 ml). The extracts were combined with the organic phase, dried over anhydrous CaCl2, and evaporated by purging with air. 5-Methyl-1-phenyl-1H-1,2,3-triazole-4-carbonyl azide (VIIb) was obtained from 4.9 g (22 mmol) of XIIb and 3.2 g (49 mmol) of sodium azide in 50 ml of water using 0.3 g of BTEAC. Yield 4.6 g (92%). Mp 88-89°C. IR spectrum, ν, cm-1: 2193 (N3), 1694 (C=O). Found, %: C 52.78; H 3.59; N 36.45. C10H8N6O. Calculated, %: C 52.63; H 3.50; N 36.84.

experimental_procedure: (6-(Benzyloxy)-2-((((4-nitrobenzyl)oxy)carbonyl)amino)-9H-purin-9-yl)methyl Pivalate (6). To a stirred solution of (2-amino-6-(benzyloxy)-9H-purin-9-yl)methyl pivalate (4) (1.06 g, 3 mmol) and dry pyridine (3 mL) in 70 mL of anhydrous dichloromethane was added a 20% solution of phosgene in toluene (1.5 mL, 3.4 mmol) dropwise at 0-5 °C. The mixture was stirred overnight, while the ice bath was allowed to warm to room temperature. A solution of 4-nitrobenzyl alcohol (0.46 g, 3 mmol) in anhydrous dichloromethane (10 mL) was added, and the reaction mixture was stirred at room temperature for 2 h. It was then evaporated with 5 g of silica gel to dryness in vacuo and the residue was purified by column chromatography (silica gel, dichloromethane ethanol, 30:1) to give the title compound Yield 1.42 g, 89%, white solid. mp 146-148 °C; 1H NMR (CDCl3, 90 MHz) δ 10.20 (s, D2O exchangeable,1H), 8.24 (d, J = 8.5 Hz, 2H), 8.03 (s, 1H), 7.337.61 (m, 7H), 6.08 (s, 2H), 5.62 (s, 2H), 5.37 (s, 2H), 1.16 (s, 9H); MS m/z 535 [M + H]+.

experimental_procedure: Methyl N-(Methoxycarbonyl)-L-prolinate (2j) A soln of L-proline (1; 2.16 g, 18.8 mmol, 1.0 equiv) in MeOH (40 mL) was cooled to 0 °C and treated with Et3N (7.9 mL, 56.4 mmol, 3.0 equiv) before MocCl (4.1 mL, 52.6 mmol, 2.8 equiv) was added dropwise. authors: Padiya, Kamlesh J.; Gavade, Sandip; Kardile, Bhavana; Tiwari, Manojkumar; Bajare, Swapnil; Mane, Madhav; Gaware, Vivek; Varghese, Shaji; Harel, Dipak; Kurhade, Suresh
reference: Unprecedented "In Water" Imidazole Carbonylation: Paradigm Shift for Preparation of Urea and Carbamate | Padiya, Kamlesh J.; Gavade, Sandip; Kardile, Bhavana; Tiwari, Manojkumar; Bajare, Swapnil; Mane, Madhav; Gaware, Vivek; Varghese, Shaji; Harel, Dipak; Kurhade, Suresh | Organic Letters (2012), 14(11), 2814-2817
experimental_procedure: General/Typical Procedure: General Procedure for preparation of Urea / Carbamate / Thiocarbamate:-Amine (1 mmol) was taken in water at room temperature and stirred at 0°C. CDI (1.2 mmol) was added in reaction mixture at 0°C. Reaction mixture was stirred at 0°C for 1 hr and then warm upto room temperature. Reaction was monitored with TLC. After complete formation of carbonylimidazolide, nucleophile (R-NH2/R-OH/R-SH) (1.2 mmol) was added. Reaction mixture was stirred at room temperature and monitored by TLC. In most cases complete conversion was observed within 2 h. Reaction mixture was filtered; precipitate obtained was washed with cold water and dried. In case if there's no precipitation of product, reaction mixture was extracted with 3 to 4 times by ethyl acetate. Organic layer was washed thrice with water, dried over sodium sulphate, evaporated in vacuu, and purified by column chromatography. Compound 3a, Yield: 75%. CDI (12 mmol) was added to the solution of amine (10 mmol) in water at 0 °C and monitored by TLC. The reaction mixture was then warmed up to room temperature. Phenol or thiophenol (12 mmol) was added. The reaction mixture was stirred at room temperature and was monitored by TLC. 1H NMR (DMSO-d6, 300MHz): δ = 10.13 (s, 1 H), 8.27 (s, 1 H), 7.81 (dd, J = 8.9, 2.8 Hz, 1 H), 7.14 (d, J = 9.1 Hz, 2 H), 6.95 (d, J = 9.4 Hz, 2 H), 6.82 (d, J = 9.1 Hz, 1 H), 3.81 (s, 3 H), 3.76 ppm (s, 3 H). MW: 274.3.

experimental_procedure: General/Typical Procedure: General Procedure 2 for the Preparation of Ureas from Carbamates: 1-(3,4-Dimethoxyphenethyl)-3-ethylurea 9: Into a flame-dried 10 mL CEM microwave reaction vessel was added 4-methyl-2- hydroxyquinoline (MeHYQ) (32 mg, 0.20 mmol), 3,4- dimethoxyphenethylamine (171 μL, 1.00 mmol), and Nethylurethane (133 μL, 1.10 mmol). reference: Synthesis and structure of N-substituted (1-ferrocenylethyl)amine derivatives | Cakic Semencic, Mojca; Dropucic, Maja; Barisic, Lidija; Molcanov, Kresimir; Rapic, Vladimir | Structural Chemistry (2007), 18(3), 273-278
experimental_procedure: N-acetyl-N-ethoxycarbonyl-(1-ferrocenylethyl)amine (6) n-BuLi (1.6 M in hexane, 1 mmol) was added to a cold (−25 °C) solution of bromo-amide 4 (0.5 mmol) in dry THF (5 ml) and stirred at −25 °C for 2 hours. After that ClCOOEt (0.6 mmol) was added and mixture was stirred for an additional hour at the same temperature, poured into the water, extracted with CH2Cl2, washed with saturated aqueous solution of NaCl, dried, and evaporated. TLC-purification of crude product with CH2Cl2/ diethyl ether (15 : 1). yellow product 6, yield: 154 mg (77%) IR (CH2Cl2) νmax/cm−1: 1734 (C=O, COOEt), 1693 (C=O, COCH3). 1H-NMR (CDCl3) δ/ppm: 5.9 (q, 1H, CH), 4.05–4.3 (m, 11H, 9HFc + CH2), 2.41 (s, 3H,COCH3), 1.64 (s, 3H, CHCH3), 1.18 (t, 3H, CH2CH3, 3J = 7.2 Hz).13C-NMR, APT (CDCl3) δ/ppm: 172.28 (COCH3), 154.67 (COOEt), 88.43 (C-1, Fc), 70.41 (Cpunsubst), 69.96 (C-3, Fc), 69.29 (C-4, Fc), 69.0 (C-2, Fc), 67.53 (C-5, Fc), 62.34 (CH2), 49.26 (CHCH3), 29.54 (COCH3), 17.43 (CHCH3), 13.76 (CH2CH3). HR-MS: calc. for C17H21NO3Fe = 343.08710, found: 343.08700. MS (EI): m/z = 343 (100) [M]+, 301 (5) [M+ −Ac], 271 (5) [M+ −COOEt], 251 (17) [M+ −CpCHMe], 166 (69), 163 (41) [FeCpCHMeNH], 121 (35) [CpFe], 91 (20) [CpCHMe], 56 (10) [Fe]. Crystallographic data: C17H21FeNO3, Formula (wt./g mol−1) 343.20, Crystal dimensions/mm 0.2x0.15x0.1, Space group P21/n, a (Å) 14.1895(6), b (Å) 7.9961(3), c (Å) 14.4287(5), α (°) 90, β (°) 96.163(3), γ (°) 90.
notes: chemoselective, in-situ generated reactant in stage 1

authors: Donald, James R.; Wood, Rebekah R.; Martin, Stephen F.
reference: Application of a Sequential Multicomponent Assembly Process/Huisgen Cycloaddition Strategy to the Preparation of Libraries of 1,2,3-Triazole-Fused 1,4-Benzodiazepines | Donald, James R.; Wood, Rebekah R.; Martin, Stephen F. | ACS Combinatorial Science (2012), 14(2), 135-143
experimental_procedure: General/Typical Procedure: 1-(4H-Benzo[f][1,2,3]triazolo[1,5-a][1,4]diazepin-5(6H)-yl)-2-methoxyethanone (8{2}). Methoxyacetyl chloride (20{2}) (39 µL, 0.43 mmol) was added to a solution of amine 6 (40 mg, 0.21 mmol) and triethylamine (90 µL, 0.64 mmol) in anhydrous CH2Cl2 (1.0 mL), and the reaction was stirred at room temperature for 3 h. The mixture was diluted with CH2Cl2 (20 mL) and washed with aqueous HCl (10 mL, 1.0 M) and saturated aqueous NaHCO3 (10 mL). The organic layer was dried (MgSO4) and concentrated under reduced pressure, and the residue was purified by flash chromatography eluting with EtOAc. Product: 32{1,13}; Yield:88%. Molecular Weight: 394.47%.

experimental_procedure: General/Typical Procedure: 4-(2-Aminoethyl)-N-(9-fluorenylmethoxycarbonyl)phenylamine Hydrochloride (1b); Typical Procedure To a soln of 4-aminophenethylamine (0.3 g, 2.3 mmol) in 10% aq AcOH (20 mL) was added FmocCl (0.6 g, 2.4 mmol) dissolved in 1,4-dioxane (20 mL). After overnight stirring at r.t., Et2O (2 × 30 mL) was added to the reaction mixture to extract the nonpolar impurities. The reaction mixture was then acidified with 2 N HCl to pH 1. The precipitate was collected by filtration, washed with Et2O (15 mL) and dried under reduced pressure overnight. 4-(Aminomethyl)-N-(9-fluorenylmethoxycarbonyl)phenylamine Hydrochloride (Entry 3) White solid; yield: 93%. experimental_procedure: General/Typical Procedure: Synthesis of Methyl 2-Aryl-ethyl/3-Aryl-propyl-carbamate. A Typical Procedure: Synthesis of Phenetylcarbamic Acid Methyl Ester 1a. To a solution of phenethylamine (1.0 mL, 8.0 mmol) and triethylamine (1.2 mL, 8.8 mmol, 1.1 equiv) in DMF (30 mL), methyl chloroformate (0.68 mL, 8.8 mmol, 1.1 equiv) were slowly added at 0 °C, and the reaction mixture was stirred at 25 °C for 1 h. Then, water (100 mL) was added, and the whole was extracted with AcOEt. The organic phase was washed with brine, dried over Na2SO4, and the solvent was evaporated under reduced pressure to give a residue, which was column-chromatographed on silica gel (eluent/AcOEt-n-hexane (1:3)) to afford phenetylcarbamic acid methyl ester 1a. Synthesis of 2-4-Tolylethylcarbamic Acid Methyl Ester 1b. Yield 93%. Colorless needles. Mp: 37.5-39.5 °C (recrystallized from hexane and dichloromethane). 1H NMR (400 MHz, CDCl3) δ (ppm): 7.12 (d, J = 8.0 Hz, 2H), 7.08 (d, J = 8.0 Hz, 2H), 4.67 (brs, 1H), 3.65 (s, 3H), 3.42 (q, J = 6.4 Hz, 2H), 2.77 (t, J = 6.8 Hz, 2H), 2.32 (s, 3H). 13C NMR (100 MHz, CDCl3) δ: 156.8, 135.7, 135.5, 129.0, 128.4, 51.7, 42.1, 35.5, 20.8. experimental_procedure: General/Typical Procedure: General procedure for substituted benzo[d]thiazol-2-yl carbamate 4a-g and 5a-g. Substituted 2-amino benzothiazole (3a-g) (0.1 mmol), was dissolved in a 80 ml of dry dichloromethane containing pyridine (0.1 mmol). To this solution was added ethyl chloroformate (for 4a-g) or phenyl chloroformate (0.1 mmol) (for 5a-g) and the reaction mixture was refluxed for 6 h. The reaction mixture was then diluted with dichloromethane (200 ml) and washed with portion of 1 M sodium bicarbonate solution, followed by water and then brine. The organic layer was collected and dried over sodium sulfate. The solvent was removed under reduced pressure to yield the product which was recrystallized from toluene: methanol mixture. Compound: 4g, Yield: 75 %. experimental_procedure: General/Typical Procedure: N-Benzyloxycarbonyl-4-pentenamine (2a) To a suspension of LiAlH4 (1.13 g, 29.8 mmol) in Et2O (30 mL) at room temperature, 4-pentenenitrile (0.99 mL, 9.94 mmol) was added dropwise. After heating under reflux for two hours (monitored by TLC) the mixture was allowed to reach room temperature. Then, Na2SO4·10H2O was added to the mixture with vigorous stirring until grey LiAlH4 salts turned into white. The suspension was filtered off through a sort pad of Celite® and concentrated under vacuum. experimental_procedure: A. General procedure for preparation of substrate 1 (1d as representative Example) To a round bottom flask equipped with magnetic stir bar, L-tyrosine (200 mg, 1.2 mmol) was added and dissolved in DMF (8.0 mL, 0.15 M) followed by the addition of EtN3 (157 mg, 1.56 mmol, 1.3 eq.) and DMAP (7.5 mg, 0.06 mmol, 0.05 eq.). The mixture was diluted with EtOAc (100 mL) and washed by HCl solution (1.0 M), saturated NaHCO3 (aq.), brine and then dried over anhydrous Na2SO4. The solvent was removed under reduced pressure to provide the crude residue. experimental_procedure: General/Typical Procedure: To 1 mmol of an amine, 1 mmol of the protecting group [CBzCl, 50% solution in toluene or (Boc)2O] was added dropwise, followed by 10 mol% of Me2SBr2 catalyst. reference: Synthesis and structure of di[methoxy(ethoxy)carbonylamino-1H-benzimidazol-5-yl] ethers | Pilyugin, V. S.; Sapozhnikov, Yu. E.; Kiseleva, G. V.; Sapozhnikova, N. A.; Vorob'eva, T. P.; Klimakova, E. V. | Russian Journal of General Chemistry (2005), 75(10), 1509-1513
experimental_procedure: To 1.0 l of water we added with stirring 140 g of the finely dispersed crude product containing 48.77% sodium cyanamide. To the resulting suspension we gradually added with vigorous stirring at 20-30°C 73.33 g of methyl chloroformate, avoiding overheating of the reaction mixture above 30°C. The molar ratio of sodium cyanamide to methyl chloroformate was 1 : 1. After adding the whole amount of methyl chloroformate, the mixture was vigorously stirred at 30-35°C for an additional 15-20 min to complete formation of methyl cyanocarbamate sodium salt. The sulfide ions were separated by adding 125.23 g of zinc sulfate. The mixture was stirred, and the precipitate of zinc sulfide (75.57 g) was filtered off. Then the mixture was acidified with HCl to pH 3.5-4.5. To the resulting solution of methyl cyanocarbamate we added 67.72 g of tetraamine IX; the mixture was heated to 90-95°C with stirring. The molar ratio sodium cyanamide : methyl chloroformate : tetraaminodiphenyl ether IX was 2.6 : 2.6 : 1.0. Under these conditions, the reaction was complete in 6-7 h. To bind the released ammonia, we gradually added hydrochloric acid to the reaction mixture, keeping pH 3.5-4.5. The resulting precipitate of I was thoroughly washed on the filter to remove salts and dried on a vacuum roller drier. Di(methoxycarbonylamino-1H-benzimidazol-5-yl) ether I, yield 96.44 g, 82%.

experimental_procedure: General/Typical Procedure: A. General procedure for preparation of substrate 1 (1d as representative Example) To a round bottom flask equipped with magnetic stir bar, L-tyrosine (200 mg, 1.2 mmol) was added and dissolved in DMF (8.0 mL, 0.15 M) followed by the addition of EtN3 (157 mg, 1.56 mmol, 1.3 eq.) and DMAP (7.5 mg, 0.06 mmol, 0.05 eq.). The reaction flask was cooled in ice water for 15 minutes and CbzCl (224 mg, 1.32 mmol, 1.1 eq.) was added drop wise over 5 minutes. The reaction was monitored by TLC and until the starting material was consumed over 5 hours. The mixture was diluted with EtOAc (100 mL) and washed by HCl solution (1.0 M), saturated NaHCO3 (aq.), brine and then dried over anhydrous Na2SO4. The solvent was removed under reduced pressure to give the crude residue. The amino alcohol was then dissolved in dry THF (6.0 mL, 0.15 M) and methyl allyl carbonate (157 mg, 1.35 mmol, 1.5 eq.) and the palladium catalyst (52 mg, 0.045 mmol, 0.05 eq.) were added. The solution was kept under argon protection and heated to 60 °C for 5 hours. Once TLC indicated the completion of the reaction, the mixture was diluted with EtOAc (100 mL). The organic phase was washed by HCl solution (1.0 M), saturated NaHCO3 (aq.) and brine and then dried over anhydrous Na2SO4. The solvent was removed under reduced pressure to provide the crude residue. Flash silica gel chromatography (Ethyl Acetate/Hexane 10:90) was then applied to give 294 mg (92%) of the allyl ether intermediate. The allyl ether (294 mg, 0.83 mmol) was then dissolved in dichloromethane (4 mL, 0.2 M). MVK (290 mg, 4.15 mmol, 5.0 equiv.) was added in under argon protection. Hoveyda-Grubbs II catalyst (10 mg, 0.016 mmol, 0.02 equiv.) was added in the reaction mixture. The reaction mixture was then warmed up to 45 °C and kept stirring for 4 hours, until the TLC indicated the completion of reaction. The solvent was removed under reduced pressure to give a residue. Flash silica gel chromatography (Ethyl Acetate/Hexane 25:75) was then applied to give the intramolecular aza-Michael precursor 1d 554 mg, yield 90%.
